minutes.headline: Assessors debated a resident's request to rerun property-card changes, deferring to town counsel's opinion; no decision was reached.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard the principal assessor's status report, then spent most of the meeting on a resident's request for simulations showing how six property-card changes affected his abated assessment. The board said it would wait for town counsel's opinion. It also signed abatements and commitments, approved the June 10 executive session minutes as amended, voted to publish the website without three components, set tentative September meeting dates, and went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the board for the abatement granted in May, asked when the check would arrive, and asked for a working session to learn how property-card factors affected his abated assessment.

Said he is not seeking access to the software, only printouts showing the incremental impact of six property-card changes (fireplace, kitchen, bathroom, foundation, effective year built, percent good). Argued this falls within the assessor's job description.

votes.motion: Accept the June 10 executive session minutes as amended by Sarah.
Accept the June 10, 2024 minutes with Mr. rabbit's addition that a member may abstain and participate in the conversation, plus typo corrections.
Publish the website as it is, pulling the ISO reference, org chart/work breakdown structure and site map, to be added later as agreed.
Suspend open meeting and enter executive session under purpose 7 (c.59 s.60, abatement applications).

budget_items.topic: Motor vehicle excise commitment number three
budget_items.what_was_said: The assessor reported the commitment's bills and total, mailed July 22.
Six supplemental bills awaited board approval that night.
Residential and commercial new growth was reported as assessed value, not tax. Personal property and utility growth were still pending with the consultant.
Invoices were signed for the software annual fee, a Vision report on the LA3, and two other invoices.
A negative abatement total was questioned and explained as reversals and payments already made.

budget_items.topic: Effect of the property card changes on building value
budget_items.what_was_said: The resident said the changes he listed had only a small impact on the building value and wanted to understand why.
Members discussed changes to the home value and income limits and the interest rate on deferrals.

budget_items.topic: Real estate and personal property abatements
budget_items.what_was_said: Abatements processed were signed in bulk.

decisions.decision: The board agreed that the assistant assessor stays on until December. They said any change by the interim town manager would have to be negotiated.
The board will wait for town counsel's opinion before deciding on the resident's request. If counsel allows it, staff will try to find time for the six comparisons.
The 61B withdrawal and right-of-first-refusal item was tabled until the open space committee gives a recommendation. The next meeting is in August.
The 41A deferral research will be written up and sent to the state contact for review.
The chair asked the principal assessor to take over preparing preliminary agendas and meeting logistics starting around September.
The board tentatively set September 16 and 30 as meeting dates, returning to two meetings a month.
A vote on the executive-session resident-question policy was deferred to a future discussion of board policies.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors did not decide a resident's request for simulations of six property-card changes; it will wait for town counsel's opinion.
If counsel allows it, staff will try to find time to run the six comparisons the resident asked for.
The board voted to publish its website without the ISO reference, the org chart and the site map, to be added later; the outcome was not audible.
The 61B land withdrawal and the town's right of first refusal were tabled until the open space committee gives a recommendation.
The board tentatively set September 16 and 30 as meeting dates, returning to two meetings a month, then went into executive session.

why_it_matters: A homeowner who has won an abatement may be able to see how individual property-card factors affected the assessed value, but only if town counsel says the assessors may produce those comparisons.
The 61B item bears on whether the town takes up its right of first refusal on land leaving a tax-reduced program, and it now waits on the open space committee.
watch_next: Town counsel's opinion on the resident's request for property-card comparisons.
The board's next meeting in August, and the tentative September 16 and 30 meetings.
